prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings place B048 first, but agreement is not the argument; the argument is that the discovery is a discernible change in the field. The incretin effect, the processing of proglucagon, the identification of the active truncated GLP-1 peptide and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions defined a new physiological axis, and that axis was converted into drugs used by tens of millions of patients, with independent randomized outcome trials confirming cardiovascular, renal and metabolic benefit. This is a specific discovery with a traceable chain from physiology to medicine, not a career award, and it has had enough time for its impact to be judged. I hold the three-person basic-science configuration (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) as the most defensible reading of the supplied names.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested and Mojsov's role is sometimes disputed, and other early peptide and cloning contributors (Habener has been raised by a colleague) are outside the credited list. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's long-acting analogue work is what actually produced liraglutide and semaglutide, so a prize that omits the industrial development side risks describing a physiological discovery whose clinical consequence is credited elsewhere. The three-person cap forces a choice between discovery credit and development credit that cannot be made cleanly from the supplied evidence.

responses.point: Ranks imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition (B005) second as proof that a rationally targeted kinase inhibitor can turn a fatal cancer into a chronic disease, with Lydon, Druker and Sawyers as a clear triad.
responses.response: I agree that B005 is scientifically strong and clearly mature, and I would not call it weaker than B031 on impact. My qualification is that the credited triad does not map onto the discovery as cleanly as the incretin trio does: the oncogenic BCR-ABL mechanism, on which the targeting concept rests, was established by others outside the list, so a prize to these three would credit drug discovery and translation while leaving the underlying cancer biology unrecognised. I therefore keep it below B031 and B017, but I accept that this is a close call and not a settled one.

responses.point: Places TNF blockade (B001, Feldmann and Maini) second as a clean two-person pairing that established the cytokine-targeted paradigm, while describing CAR-T (B031) as having a credit gap because Eshhar is not among the supplied names.
responses.response: The Eshhar gap is a fair and serious point against B031 and I share it; it is the main reason I do not put CAR-T forward as the preferred configuration. Where I differ is on B001: the clean pairing is attractive, but the supplied credit omits those who cloned TNF and made the antibodies, and the field has absorbed anti-TNF so long ago that I want evidence of a discernible change in the discovery itself, not only in practice. I would still take B001 seriously if the committee wants a two-person second part, but I would not rank it above B031 or B017.

responses.point: Ranks cGAS-STING (B044) fourth, with Chen and Barber as the defensible core, while noting that therapeutic translation is still maturing and recognition could be somewhat early.
responses.response: I agree with the caveat Rickard himself raises. The cGAS-STING mechanism is clear and well confirmed, but a discovery of this kind is better judged after the therapeutic or diagnostic consequence is visible, and the attribution among Chen, Barber, Ishikawa, Wu and Sun is not yet settled. I think it is a strong candidate for later years, not for a prize that already has B048 as an obvious anchor.

responses.point: Supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B048, but notes the priority questions around active GLP-1, that Habener is missing from the list, and that Knudsen's industrial work would crowd a three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and take the priority question seriously. The supplied evidence does not allow me to resolve Habener's or Mojsov's precise priority, and I will not pretend to. My reasoning for Mojsov over Knudsen is that the prize recognises the discovery and not the drug-development programme, and the active peptide form is the discovery step on which the drug programme rests. I regard this as a judgement and I am open to being persuaded otherwise if the attribution evidence shifts.

responses.point: Ranks optogenetics (B050) second and flags that the six-name field cannot be cut to three without a real weakness, while ranking TOR signalling (B016) fourth.
responses.response: I agree that the six-name optogenetics field is the central problem for B050, and I would add that clinical consequence is early, so the case rests on a research tool. That does not disqualify it, but I would not choose a three-person subset (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) when Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck all have credible claims. I keep it out of my alternatives for that reason.

uncertainties: Who first identified and characterised the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is not resolved by the supplied evidence, and Habener is outside the credited list.
Whether a three-person limit should favour physiological discovery over industrial drug development, which affects the inclusion of Mojsov versus Knudsen.
Whether CAR-T (B031) can be given a defensible credit set without Eshhar, and whether UPR (B017) is better judged as a stand-alone second achievement alongside incretins.
Whether a two-part prize would dilute the clarity of the incretin case or would give fairer recognition to a basic-science discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted candidate. My own field (nuclear receptors, dopamine neuron development) does not overlap with the shortlisted discoveries, and my documented collaboration with Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson and my co-authorship with Per Svenningsson and Abdel El Manira do not involve any credited name on the shortlist. I flag these only for transparency.
